season: Kharif — nursery in June, transplant July, harvest Oct-Nov.
soil: Clayey loam that holds standing water; pH 5.5-7.0.
irrigation: Keep 2-5cm standing water through tillering; drain 10 days before harvest. Alternate wetting-and-drying (AWD) can cut water use by ~25% with no yield loss.
pest: Stem borer and leaf folder are common. Use pheromone traps and encourage natural predators before chemical sprays; remove and destroy affected tillers.
fertilizer: Split nitrogen across basal, tillering, and panicle-initiation stages; get soil tested locally for exact NPK ratio.
sustain: AWD irrigation and SRI reduce both water use and methane emissions from paddies.

season: Rabi — sow late Oct to mid-Nov, harvest March-April.
irrigation: Critical stages: crown-root initiation (20-25 days after sowing), tillering, grain-filling.
pest: Aphids and yellow rust in humid, cool weather. Early sowing and resistant varieties reduce rust pressure.
fertilizer: Split nitrogen between basal and first irrigation; phosphorus/potash usually fully basal — confirm with soil-test recommendation.
sustain: Zero-tillage sowing after paddy cuts fuel use and preserves soil moisture and organic matter.

season: Kharif — sow May-June or with monsoon onset; harvest Oct-Jan in stages.
irrigation: Drip irrigation with mulching cuts water use significantly versus flood irrigation.
pest: Pink bollworm and whitefly are major threats. Pheromone traps, timely sowing, destroying crop residue after harvest, and avoiding excess nitrogen help.
fertilizer: Nutrient-hungry — staggered nitrogen plus adequate potash for boll development; soil test guides exact schedule.
sustain: Intercropping with pulses (e.g. moong) improves soil nitrogen and gives a second income stream.

season: Planted Oct-Nov (adsali) or Feb-March (suru); 10-18 month duration.
soil: Deep, well-drained loam to clay-loam; pH 6.5-7.5.
irrigation: Very water-intensive — drip irrigation cuts water use ~30-40% versus furrow irrigation while improving yield.
pest: Early shoot borer and whitefly common; trash mulching suppresses weeds and conserves moisture.
fertilizer: Heavy feeder of nitrogen and potash; split doses at planting, tillering, and grand-growth stage.
sustain: Trash mulching instead of burning returns organic matter to soil and avoids stubble-burning air pollution.

season: Kharif — sow with monsoon onset (June-July), harvest Sept-Oct.
soil: Well-drained loam, low waterlogging tolerance; pH 6.0-7.5.
irrigation: Mostly rainfed; protective irrigation at flowering and pod-filling if there's a dry spell.
pest: Girdle beetle and stem fly attack young plants; timely sowing and seed treatment reduce early infestation.
fertilizer: Legume — fixes some nitrogen; Rhizobium seed inoculation reduces nitrogen fertilizer needed.
sustain: Good rotation partner after cotton or sugarcane, improving soil nitrogen for the next crop.

season: Kharif — sow June-July, harvest Dec-Jan (long duration).
irrigation: Deep-rooted, largely rainfed; one irrigation at pod-formation stage helps in dry seasons.
pest: Pod borer (Helicoverpa) is key — pheromone traps and bird perches before spraying.
fertilizer: Low requirement as a legume; light basal phosphorus is usually enough.
sustain: Deep roots break soil hardpan; leaf litter adds organic matter to degraded or marginal soils.

season: Rabi (main), also Kharif and late-Kharif; ~90-120 days to harvest.
soil: Well-drained sandy loam; pH 6.0-7.0; sensitive to waterlogging.
irrigation: Light, frequent irrigation — drip with mulch keeps bulb rot low and improves bulb size.
pest: Thrips dominant, especially hot dry weather; blue sticky traps and timely irrigation help.
fertilizer: Needs adequate sulphur and potash for bulb quality, alongside split nitrogen doses.
sustain: Drip plus mulch cuts water use and reduces purple blotch disease pressure from overhead irrigation.

season: Grown nearly year-round with irrigation; ~25-day nursery, 60-90 days to first harvest.
soil: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter; pH 6.0-6.8.
irrigation: Drip with staking/mulching reduces fruit cracking and soil-borne disease.
pest: Fruit borer and whitefly (spreads leaf-curl virus); yellow sticky traps, staking for airflow, remove infected plants early.
fertilizer: Calcium deficiency causes blossom-end rot — ensure adequate calcium with balanced NPK.
sustain: Staking and mulching reduce water use and fungicide need by improving airflow.

season: Kharif and Rabi both possible with irrigation; harvest starts ~75-90 days after transplant.
irrigation: Drip irrigation reduces fruit-rot and root-rot risk from waterlogged flood irrigation.
pest: Thrips and mites cause leaf curl; reflective mulch and removing affected leaves help.
fertilizer: Needs steady potash through fruiting for pungency and shelf life.
sustain: Intercropping with marigold can trap certain pest species away from the main crop.

season: Kharif (June-July) and summer crop under irrigation; ~100-130 days.
soil: Well-drained sandy loam essential for pod development; pH 6.0-6.5.
irrigation: Critical stages: flowering, pegging, pod development — moisture stress at pegging sharply cuts yield.
pest: Leaf miner and white grub common; deep summer ploughing exposes grubs to predators and sun.
fertilizer: Legume — fixes much of its own nitrogen; gypsum at flowering improves pod-filling.
sustain: Residue is good fodder; nitrogen-fixing improves soil for the following cereal crop.

season: Kharif (June) or Rabi/spring with irrigation; ~90-110 days.
irrigation: Most water-sensitive at tasseling/silking — shortfall here has the largest yield impact.
pest: Fall armyworm now major across Maharashtra; scout weekly for window-pane leaf damage, act promptly.
fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder — split across basal, knee-high, and tasseling stages.
sustain: Maize-legume intercropping improves nitrogen use and gives ground cover against soil erosion.

season: Kharif, sown with monsoon onset; ~75-90 days.
irrigation: Highly drought-tolerant; usually grown rainfed, good for water-scarce regions.
pest: Downy mildew in wet years and shoot fly early; resistant varieties are most effective.
fertilizer: Low input crop; light basal dose generally sufficient.
sustain: Highly climate-resilient staple — good hedge against erratic monsoons.

season: Kharif and Rabi both grown in Maharashtra; ~100-120 days.
soil: Wide tolerance including moderately saline soils; pH 6.0-8.5.
irrigation: Drought-tolerant, deep root system; Rabi jowar relies mostly on residual soil moisture.
pest: Shoot fly and stem borer in seedling stage; timely sowing after first good rain reduces risk.
fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen need, split between basal and post-thinning stage.
sustain: Traditional low-water staple — supports nutrition security and climate resilience.

soil: Well-drained loam to clay-loam; pH 6.0-7.5; poor in waterlogged fields.
irrigation: Largely rainfed on residual moisture; one light irrigation at pod-development stage lifts yield.
pest: Pod borer (Helicoverpa) key pest — bird perches and pheromone traps; avoid spraying during flowering to protect pollinators.
fertilizer: Legume — needs little nitrogen; light phosphorus basal dose plus Rhizobium seed treatment.
sustain: Excellent rotation crop after Kharif cotton or soybean — restores soil nitrogen cheaply.

season: Pruned twice a year (April/October); harvest ~90-120 days after fruit pruning.
soil: Well-drained, deep soil; pH 6.5-7.5; poor drainage causes root rot.
irrigation: Drip near-universal in Maharashtra's grape belts; deficit irrigation before harvest improves sugar content.
pest: Downy mildew in humid weather and thrips; canopy management for airflow reduces fungal pressure.
fertilizer: Needs balanced micronutrients (zinc, boron) alongside NPK — petiole analysis used commercially.
sustain: Drip irrigation plus canopy management cuts water use and fungicide frequency.

season: Can flower up to three times a year (Mrig/Hasta/Ambe bahar); ~150-180 days fruit development.
soil: Tolerates light, well-drained, even moderately saline soils; pH 6.5-7.5.
irrigation: Drip with a planned dry period before flower induction ('bahar treatment') is standard practice.
pest: Bacterial blight and fruit borer biggest threats; orchard sanitation is most effective non-chemical control.
fertilizer: Organic manure plus balanced NPK through drip fertigation is common commercial approach.
sustain: Suited to drought-prone, marginal land — climate-resilient option where water-hungry crops struggle.
